record.paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Gray-Scott spot dynamics on the sphere
record.original_question: For the Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion model on the unit sphere, v_t = epsilon^2 Delta_S v - v + B u v^2 and tau u_t = D Delta_S u + (1 - u) - u v^2, in the singular limit epsilon -> 0 with B = O(epsilon/nu) and nu = -1/log(epsilon), the derived slow dynamics for localized spots couples spot locations x_j and strengths S_j through the reduced-wave Green function G satisfying Delta_S G - D^{-1}G = -delta(x - xi) and G(x; xi) approximately -(1/(2pi)) log|x - xi| + R near xi. How can one investigate the dynamics and equilibria of localized spot patterns on the sphere for this Gray-Scott DAE when the reduced-wave Green function and its regular part R are not available in a simple explicit form?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion system on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb{R}^3$:
$$v_t = \varepsilon^2 \Delta_S v - v + B\, u v^2, \qquad \tau u_t = D\, \Delta_S u + (1-u) - u v^2,$$
where $\Delta_S$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $S^2$, $D>0$ and $\tau>0$ are fixed, and the feed parameter scales as $B = O(\varepsilon/\nu)$ with $\nu = -1/\log\varepsilon$, in the singular limit $\varepsilon\to 0^+$. In this limit the activator $v$ concentrates near $N$ localized spots at points $x_1(t),\dots,x_N(t)\in S^2$ with strengths $S_1(t),\dots,S_N(t)$. Standard matched-asymptotic analysis yields a differential-algebraic system (DAE) coupling the spot locations $x_j$ and strengths $S_j$ via the reduced-wave Green function $G(x;\xi)$ on $S^2$, defined as the unique solution of
$$\Delta_S G(x;\xi) - D^{-1} G(x;\xi) = -\delta_{S^2}(x-\xi), \qquad x\in S^2,$$
with local behavior $G(x;\xi) = -\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\log|x-\xi| + R(\xi) + o(1)$ as $x\to\xi$, where $R(\xi)$ is the regular part and $|x-\xi|$ denotes the chordal (Euclidean) distance in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Develop a tractable theoretical and computational framework to analyze the slow dynamics, equilibrium configurations (ring patterns, polyhedral configurations, etc.), and linear stability of $N$-spot quasi-equilibrium patterns governed by this DAE in the case where $G(x;\xi)$ and its regular part $R(\xi)$ are not available in simple closed form. Specifically: characterize the equilibrium spot configurations $\{x_j^\ast\}$ and equal-strength equilibria, classify their stability with respect to translational, amplitude, and shape (peanut-splitting) modes, and identify possible bifurcations as $D$, $N$, and the feed strength vary.
artifact.category_tag: Localized spot patterns on the sphere
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open direction in work on localized spot patterns for reaction–diffusion systems on the sphere. Subsequent literature (Trinh–Ward and related work on the Brusselator/Schnakenberg on the sphere) has developed numerical-asymptotic frameworks using approximations of the reduced-wave Green function, but a complete analytical theory of Gray–Scott spot equilibria, slow dynamics, and stability on the sphere with the reduced-wave Green function (rather than its Laplace–Beltrami simplification) remains incomplete and is generally treated as still open.

status_evidence.title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Slow dynamics of spots on the unit sphere for the Gray-Scott model; further investigation of the reduced-wave Green function case is identified as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Gray-Scott spot dynamics on the sphere with reduced-wave Green function is identified as requiring further investigation.

status_evidence.title: The Stability and Dynamics of Localized Spot Patterns in the Two-Dimensional Gray-Scott Model
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid asymptotic-numerical method for spot DAE dynamics in 2D; the spherical case with the reduced-wave Green function is not treated here.
status_evidence.claim: The planar Gray-Scott DAE has been analyzed, but the spherical reduced-wave Green function setting remains an extension.
